intro: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark told the IMF and World Bank that the technological singularity has begun — and Wall Street seems to be having an existential crisis of its own about it, with CoreWeave's bonds hitting distressed levels and investors openly asking whether the trillion-dollar AI boom is built on sand. Today's digest spans that full spectrum of AI confidence and doubt, from OpenAI's breakthrough in teaching models to write COBOL to a Guardian columnist arguing the whole thing is just generating expensive slop, plus Hollywood's first fictional AI actress, a Plex exploit chain built with AI assistance, and NYC's mayor telling his city to push back against all of it.

stories.title: Creator Brooke Lacey demos AI-powered TikTok editing workflow on 'How I AI' podcast
stories.summary: Content creator Brooke Lacey, with over 290,000 TikTok followers and 25+ years in tech, demonstrated on the 'How I AI' podcast how she uses Claude Code combined with FFmpeg and OpenAI's Whisper to automatically edit TikTok videos, turning raw phone footage into captioned, jump-cut clips in about 15 seconds. She taught Claude her specific editing cadence, hook style, and humor. She also mines TikTok comments for script ideas and maintains a weekly posting schedule with no human editor. The newsletter issue also covered a separate episode where Claire tested Meta's Muse Wonder model across nearly 20 tasks, finding it excels at agentic work like billing support and inbox triage but fails at frontend design and video editing.
stories.opinion: A compelling real-world example of AI augmenting creative work rather than replacing it—Lacey's workflow shows the sweet spot where AI handles tedious editing mechanics while the creator retains full artistic control.

stories.title: Actively exploited Plex Media Server vulnerabilities enable remote code execution
stories.summary: Recently patched Plex Media Server vulnerabilities are being actively exploited in the wild. A researcher developed 'Plex2Shell,' an exploit chain combining four CVEs (one rated 8.6/10) to achieve remote code execution via unauthenticated SSRF, loopback pivot, security token theft, and payload delivery. A honeypot detected active scanning and successful infections within a day, with attackers installing cryptominers and residential proxy software. The vulnerabilities were fixed in Plex version 1.43.3 released at the start of last month. The original researcher noted heavy use of AI in developing the exploit chain, though emphasized hours of iterative human-guided work were required.
stories.opinion: A timely reminder that media servers exposed to the internet are high-value targets—and that AI is accelerating the exploit development timeline, making prompt patching even more critical.

stories.title: AI-generated actors edge toward Hollywood film roles
stories.summary: Two notable cases highlight the growing use of AI-generated actors in Hollywood: a digital recreation of young Val Kilmer starring in the western 'As Deep as the Grave,' and an entirely fictional AI-created actress named Tilly Norwood set for her feature film debut. Industry experts remain divided on whether AI actors replacing or supplementing real performers is imminent or still far off, with questions about the uncanny valley effect, actors' rights, and broader implications for the film industry.
stories.opinion: The Val Kilmer recreation and fictional AI actress represent two very different propositions—resurrecting a consenting actor's likeness versus creating synthetic performers wholesale—and each raises distinct ethical and legal questions the industry hasn't resolved.

stories.title: Former SJSU volleyball coach files renewed lawsuit alleging retaliation over transgender athlete opposition
stories.summary: A former assistant women's volleyball coach at San José State University filed a renewed lawsuit in October 2026 alleging her dismissal constituted sex discrimination and violated her First and Fourteenth Amendment rights. The coach, who opposed the inclusion of a transgender player on religious grounds, claims she was monitored, suspended, and ultimately not renewed after filing a Title IX complaint and speaking to the media. The case was previously transferred between federal districts. The Trump administration had earlier concluded SJSU violated Title IX in its handling of the situation.
stories.opinion: This case sits at the intersection of religious liberty, transgender inclusion, and employment retaliation law, and its outcome could set significant precedent for how institutions navigate competing Title IX claims.

stories.title: HBR: AI marketing transformations will get harder before they get easier
stories.summary: Harvard Business Review argues that organizations adopting AI for marketing should expect the transformation process to become more difficult before yielding results, outlining both the challenges and eventual benefits of the transition.
stories.opinion: A sensible framing that counters the hype cycle—most organizational transformations follow a J-curve, and AI marketing adoption is no exception.

stories.title: OpenAI reports major gains in AI coding for COBOL, Fortran, and other low-resource languages
stories.summary: OpenAI describes improvements to their models for low-resource programming languages like COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic. They introduce two evaluations: MultiLangBench (building a SQLite-compatible database engine in 20 languages) and a COBOL migration benchmark. GPT-6 Astra reaches 87.4% average test pass rate on MultiLangBench (up from 26.8% for GPT-5.6 Sol), and GPT-6.1 Sol achieves 97.9% accuracy on COBOL migration at high reasoning effort (up from 5.4%). They emphasize these languages underpin critical infrastructure in banking, weather forecasting, and nuclear safety.
stories.opinion: Potentially one of the highest-impact practical applications of AI coding—the organizations most desperate for help maintaining legacy COBOL and Fortran systems are exactly those least able to recruit developers who know those languages.

stories.title: NYC Mayor Mamdani urges local resistance to AI, criticizes federal 'abdication' on regulation
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, speaking at an AI Now Institute event with activist Ilana Glazer, urged New Yorkers to resist the narrative that AI's takeover of jobs, education, and daily life is inevitable. He criticized the federal government's 'complete abdication' on AI regulation and its framing of AI as an arms race with China. Mamdani pointed to his recent actions—banning AI in elementary and middle schools and requiring disclosure of AI-generated real estate listings—as examples of local pushback. He cited the U.S. military's AI-assisted strike on an Iranian school that killed over 150 people as evidence of reckless AI adoption without accountability.
stories.opinion: Mamdani is staking out a distinctive position as the most prominent elected official actively implementing AI restrictions rather than just calling for guardrails—whether the school ban and disclosure rules prove effective or merely symbolic will be the real test.

stories.title: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark declares the technological singularity has begun
stories.summary: Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark declared at the IMF and World Bank annual meetings that the technological singularity has begun, citing AI benchmark scores on Humanity's Last Exam jumping from 8% to 67.7% and FrontierMath from 2% to 94% since 2025. He presented an Anthropic model projecting U.S. GDP could reach $44 trillion by 2030 if AI adoption accelerates, while warning of significant job disruption. Clark urged nations to invest in labs and robotics infrastructure, and noted that CEO Dario Amodei has floated the idea of capping AI intelligence levels, with only 'a small number of years' to act.
stories.opinion: Clark's benchmark citations are striking but cherry-picked—test scores climbing doesn't equal the singularity by most definitions, though framing it that way at an IMF/World Bank venue is clearly designed to spur policy urgency.

stories.title: US fossil fuel infrastructure sees biggest buildout in a decade as data center demand surges
stories.summary: The US is building more fossil fuel infrastructure than it has in a decade, driven by surging electricity demand from data centers, factories, and EVs. Renewable energy growth is slowing under the Trump administration's policies favoring fossil fuels. A report by the Environmental Defense Fund and Atlas Public Policy warns that completing planned gas projects could lock in higher pollution and electricity costs for decades. Despite renewables gaining ground—wind and solar surpassed coal for the first time in 2024, and solar accounted for 81% of new capacity—the current policy environment is shifting America's energy landscape back toward fossil fuels.
stories.opinion: The irony of AI's enormous energy appetite potentially undoing climate progress deserves more attention—data centers are now one of the largest drivers of new fossil fuel demand at exactly the moment renewables were gaining dominance.

stories.title: ReactOS reaches milestone with direct NTFS installation support
stories.summary: ReactOS, the open-source project aiming for binary compatibility with Windows Server 2003, has enabled direct installation onto NTFS partitions for the first time. Previously limited to FAT32, the project added read-only NTFS support in 2016 and bootloader NTFS reading in 2022. The new driver still lacks caching, journaling, and security support, and may contain bugs. The volunteer-driven project, which has been in alpha for decades, sees this as an important step toward beta status, though the team acknowledges ReactOS may never be a fully viable Windows replacement.
stories.opinion: A genuinely impressive achievement for a volunteer project, even if ReactOS's practical relevance remains limited—the NTFS milestone removes one of the most glaring gaps that made the project feel perpetually incomplete.

stories.title: Guardian column: AI is creating floods of low-quality 'slop' that cost more time than they save
stories.summary: Guardian columnist Gaby Hinsliff argues that AI, rather than saving time as promised, is generating an overwhelming flood of low-quality content ('slop') that costs everyone more time to deal with. She critiques the UK government's enthusiasm for transforming public services with AI, suggesting that the technology creates new burdens—from overflowing inboxes to machine-generated bureaucratic noise—that offset any efficiency gains.
stories.opinion: The 'slop' framing resonates because it captures a real externality: even when AI saves the sender time, it often shifts work onto every recipient who must now filter through AI-generated volume.

stories.title: Nscale and Anthropic reportedly in talks for second $45 billion compute deal
stories.summary: Nscale and Anthropic are reportedly in talks for a second $45 billion compute deal, just over a month after announcing their first $45 billion partnership. Bloomberg reports the deal is near announcement but details could change. Both companies are also pursuing IPOs, with Anthropic expected to go public this year and Nscale seeking a $30 billion valuation despite investor pushback.
stories.opinion: A cumulative $90 billion in compute commitments between two companies both pursuing IPOs raises questions about whether these headline figures reflect firm obligations or aspirational frameworks designed to boost pre-IPO narratives.

stories.title: CoreWeave's bonds hit distressed levels as AI infrastructure debt concerns mount
stories.summary: CoreWeave's bonds fell into distressed territory with investors demanding 1,000+ basis points over government bond yields. Chamath Palihapitiya publicly questioned whether the AI buildout represents a private credit bubble, triggering a 20%+ drop in CoreWeave's shares and collateral damage across other AI stocks. CoreWeave cofounder Brannin McBee told the Financial Times the company wants investment-grade debt status to access insurer capital, which he described as 'unlimited'—a statement that spooked investors by suggesting the company plans to borrow even more.
stories.opinion: McBee's 'unlimited' capital comment was a remarkable own goal—at the exact moment investors worry about overleveraged AI infrastructure, signaling appetite for even more debt is the last thing the market needed to hear.

stories.title: Investors question whether $1 trillion AI stock boom is sustainable
stories.summary: Growing concerns are emerging about whether the massive investment in AI stocks—estimated at $1 trillion this year—may be overvalued. Following a notable drop in the Nasdaq 100, market observers are questioning whether the AI stock market boom is sustainable or built on inflated expectations, framing this as a potential reassessment moment for the sector.
stories.opinion: The trillion-dollar question is whether AI company revenues will grow into their valuations or whether we're seeing a classic pattern of infrastructure overbuild—history suggests both can be true simultaneously.

stories.title: Hugging Face policy chief warns embedded AI evaluators face major hurdles
stories.summary: Hugging Face's chief policy officer Irene Solaiman argued at TechCrunch Disrupt that embedded AI evaluators—third-party observers placed inside AI labs as an alternative to government regulation—face significant challenges. She highlighted that model benchmarking lacks reproducibility and standardization, the evaluation field is an 'evolving science' where tests become ineffective quickly, and agentic evaluations are expensive and underdeveloped. The push for embedded evaluators has been controversial, with Anthropic's hiring of Accenture as its first evaluator drawing criticism.
stories.opinion: Solaiman's critique cuts to the heart of the self-regulation debate—if we can't even standardize what 'safe' means in reproducible benchmarks, embedding evaluators inside labs risks creating accountability theater rather than real oversight.

stories.title: Illinois Governor Pritzker says AI could extend lifespans to 100 or threaten humanity like nukes
stories.summary: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker discussed AI on the Decoder podcast, expressing optimism that AI could help extend human lifespans to 100 years while warning it poses existential threats comparable to nuclear weapons. He argued that AI regulation, privacy, and data center policy are collective action problems requiring government intervention. The conversation touched on how tech and privacy issues are driving unexpected political realignment heading into the 2026 midterm elections.
stories.opinion: Pritzker's nuclear analogy is apt in one respect—like nuclear technology, AI's governance challenge is that it demands international coordination while every nation has incentives to defect.

tweet_headlines.headline: SpaceXAI engineer Lauren Tan built a pstack skill that __generates formal verification suites__ in TLA+, Kani, and Bend — and has already caught real bugs.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
SpaceXAI engineer Lauren Tan just revealed a new pstack skill that could change how we build with AI.

absolutely insane...

/create-formal-verification-skill creates a custom skill + formal verification suite based on what you need to prove about your code.

Here's what makes it powerful:

→ TLA+ to model state machines and concurrency
→ Kani to verify Rust code and catch undefined behavior
→ Bend to express proofs as laws in its type system

A normal test checks specific cases.

Formal verification checks whether critical properties hold across the system.

And Lauren has already found several bugs in SpaceXAI's code by experimenting with TLA+ and this skill.

The bigger idea?
Stop asking agents to try harder to write correct code.
Give them tools to prove their code does what you intended.

pstack v0.15.27. Still in beta.

If you're building serious AI coding workflows, this is worth paying attention to.

Read the breakdown, then try building your own verification skill ↓

tweet_headlines.author: learnwithmattc
tweet_headlines.headline: Running a site for __$0/month on Cloudflare Pages__ is doable by keeping WordPress local for content management and using Simply Static to export before deploying.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
I rebuilt Roots & Fruit as a static site that costs $0/month on Cloudflare Pages.

But I didn't ditch WordPress.

I start with my CDS (Core Design System). It has a WordPress compiler that generates a theme, stylesheets, and patterns. I've open-sourced it so you can fork it and adapt it to your own brand.

Then I build locally. When I'm ready to publish, Simply Static generates the static site, and Cursor deploys it to Cloudflare. That means that Studio is my staging. 

I really like this separation of concerns. I keep WordPress for what it's good at: content management, semantic layouts, and plugins that let me extend the site programmatically.

But I don't have to pay to host all that infrastructure, and I don't need PHP running on a public server just to serve HTML, CSS, and a little JavaScript.

WordPress is a great platform for AI-assisted web development, and I think people need to take its strengths more seriously.

My CDS + WordPress setup gives an AI agent the guidelines, components, and context it needs to build something accurate and compelling, consistently and reliably.

I wrote up the whole process, with GitHub links so you can adopt the approach and make it your own.

https://t.co/9dl9vVmooD

tweet_headlines.author: gippp69
tweet_headlines.headline: A Grok Bot hash-check prompt is said to drop __routine costs from $397 to $45 per month__ by skipping unchanged runs and batching non-urgent diffs until morning.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
Grok Bot users: paste this ONE prompt NOW before your routines burn another $350 this month

[check first, run only on diff]

1. every 5 min it compares a hash to the last run
2. nothing changed, it skips in milliseconds
3. real change, it drafts a plan and waits for your tap
4. non-urgent stuff waits until 07:00

in the video: 176 checks, 171 skipped, 4 real runs

1. full run every 5 min: $397/mo
2. hourly: $33/mo, but you're up to an hour late
3. every 5 min + check: $45/mo

copy this into your Grok Bot:

for every routine: hash check before the full run, skip if nothing changed, hold non-urgent diffs until 07:00, drafts before any send. show me the cost before and after, change nothing until I say go.

wake up for changes, not for the clock

tweet_headlines.author: gippp69
tweet_headlines.headline: Someone adapted __Boris Cherny's Claude Code workflow__ into a solo marketing agency: daily spend checks, Friday Shopify reports, and monthly ad culls — zero employees.
tweet_headlines.source_text:
Boris Cherny, the creator of Claude Code, just published how he actually uses it...

i turned his workflow into 1 prompt that runs a whole marketing agency. no team, no VA

here's the full setup step by step:

step 1 → paste the prompt from the images into Claude Code

step 2 → it builds a folder for every client with rules, data, drafts and a log

step 3 → 7:00 every morning it checks spend and flags anything off by 10%

step 4 → friday 8:00 it drafts a 3-page report with revenue pulled from Shopify

step 5 → once a month it kills the bottom 50% of ads and writes new tests

the catch: nothing goes to a client and no budget moves without your yes. it gathers, checks and drafts. you decide

week 1 it only drafts. by month 2 it makes the small changes on its own

1 person. 0 employees. the agency runs while you sleep

the full prompt is in the images, the rest of it in the comments ↓
